Thanks for the heads-up — I pulled traces for the request id rwd-20261102-7a4b and ran a local repro using the supplied payload. Findings below: 

- Symptom: requests hit a server-side 500 caused by an internal OOM in the reranker worker when handling large batches (~512). Heap spike happens during tokenization + attention matrix allocation.
- Repro: confirmed with batch_size=512; lowering to 64 prevents OOM and returns 200 consistently.
- Root cause: the current reranker build uses a single-worker allocation strategy for rerank step which multiplies memory by batch_size. A fix is in progress to stream tokenization and split batches across workers.

Immediate mitigations we recommend to Finlytics:
1) Reduce batch size to 64 in the SDK call.
2) Set client timeout to 60s and enable simple retry with exponential backoff (retry 3 times, base 500ms).
3) If you need immediate production stability, set reranker model variant to embed-reranker-v1-small (lower memory footprint) while we patch.

I've attached a heap/trace excerpt (heapdump.txt) and a repro request file (repro-req.json) used in testing. We'll schedule a patch for the streaming tokenization next week; estimated PR + canary in 3–4 business days.

I'll also add server-side rate limiting for large single-request batch sizes to fail fast with a helpful error rather than 500.

\u0014Dylan
